patterns.name: sql_syntax_in_request_argument
patterns.condition: A request argument contains SQL control syntax such as a quote followed by OR, UNION SELECT, or a SQL comment marker; match the argument value, not ordinary prose elsewhere in the log.
patterns.evidence: MITRE ATT&CK T1190 covers attempts to exploit a public-facing application; SQL control syntax in an input argument is a concrete indicator to investigate for that technique, not proof of successful exploitation.

patterns.name: script_tag_in_request_argument
patterns.condition: A request argument contains an HTML script tag opening or closing sequence, such as <script or </script, indicating possible script injection.
patterns.evidence: MITRE ATT&CK T1190 covers exploitation attempts against public-facing applications; a script tag submitted as input is a concrete web-injection indicator to investigate, not proof that the script executed.

patterns.name: repeated_parent_directory_traversal
patterns.condition: A single request argument contains two or more ../ or ..\ sequences, including URL-encoded variants such as %2e%2e%2f, suggesting repeated parent-directory traversal.
patterns.evidence: MITRE ATT&CK T1190 covers attempts to exploit public-facing applications; repeated parent-directory traversal sequences in an input are a concrete path-manipulation indicator to investigate, not proof of successful exploitation.
